subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep bootstrap-extra-files limited to recognized workspace filenames?
rationale: The current source and docs intentionally limit injected files to known bootstrap basenames, while the request would broaden deterministic system-prompt context loading and the public hook configuration contract.

options.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
options.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement is rebased and preserves path guards, budgets, docs, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and keep custom context in the existing first-class workspace filenames or separate product proposals.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context API
options.body: Leave this request open or supersede it only when maintainers choose a broader context/config design that covers custom startup files.

recommendation.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
recommendation.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement is rebased and preserves path guards, budgets, docs, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original bootstrap-extra-files PR and authored the in-PR refactor that made it a bundled hook.
